title: Three-SAT dictator versus no notable coordinates
statement: For every $\delta\in(0,1/8)$, there is a family of finite-seed sign testers for three-literal sign clauses with the following properties. The predicate set is finite; the thresholds are $\alpha=7/8+\delta$ and $\beta=1$; and the error function is half the three-SAT OXR error evaluated at the degree selected for $\delta$. This error takes values in $[0,1]$ and tends to zero as its argument approaches zero through positive values. Every test uses an allowed predicate, every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, and every function whose stable influences at parameters $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha$ plus the error at $\varepsilon$, for every dimension, every positive dimension, and every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
hypotheses_covered: The error tends to zero at zero through positive arguments
Every test uses a predicate from the specified set
Every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
Every function with all stable influences at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha$ plus the error, for $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$
The assertions hold in every positive dimension
